mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incorporation of the Foreign Parent Entity
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent company registry in the foreign investor's country of origin (e.g., Accounting and Corporate Regulatory Authority of Singapore or corresponding secretary of state registry)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille route: notarization (where required) followed by an Apostille certificate issued by the designated competent authority of the document's country of origin, accepted for direct use in China; no consular legalization. Non-Hague route: notarization followed by Consular Legalization by the Chinese Embassy or Consulate in the origin country. The two routes are parallel and mutually exclusive and must never be chained sequentially.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing / Certificate of Existence or Compliance
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Foreign investor's home-country company registry or recognized public registrar
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Apostille Convention state: the registry-issued certificate is notarized and then apostilled by the origin country's competent authority. Non-member state: the certificate is notarized and then submitted to the Chinese Embassy/Consulate for consular legalization. Apostille and consular legalization are alternative paths and cannot be combined.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Board Resolution and Power of Attorney designating the WFOE's legal representative and local filing agent
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Board of Directors of the foreign parent entity
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Board resolution signatures must be notarized by a certified notary public in the parent company's jurisdiction; thereafter, Hague Apostille by the competent authority if the origin state is a member of the Apostille Convention, or Consular Legalization by the Chinese Embassy/Consulate if the origin state is a non-member. These are mutually exclusive routes.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Articles of Association and Constitutional Documents of the Foreign Parent Entity
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Foreign parent company secretary or registered legal document custodian
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Certified copy of the Articles of Association is notarized in the origin country, then either apostilled (Hague member state) or consular legalized by the Chinese Embassy/Consulate (non-member state). No sequential chain of apostille followed by legalization is permitted.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank Reference Letter and Account History Certificate from the foreign parent's principal bank
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: The bank's authorized officer signature is notarized, after which the document follows either the Apostille path if the bank is located in a Hague Apostille Convention state, or the Consular Legalization path if the bank is in a non-member state; one path only, never both.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: All UBOs, directors, legal representatives, senior managers, authorized signatories and material shareholders must be screened pre-onboarding and continuously at 30-day intervals against UN Security Council consolidated lists, PRC MOFCOM and Ministry of Foreign Affairs restrictive measures lists, US OFAC SDN and non-SDN lists, EU and UK consolidated sanctions, and China's domestic abnormal-operations and administrative penalty registries. Enhanced due diligence is mandatory for foreign PEPs, domestic prominent public officials, and their family members and close associates; adverse media and sanctions-evasion typologies, including shell-company chains and virtual-card loading anomalies, must trigger escalation to the AML compliance officer within 48 hours.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: National Enterprise Credit Information Publicity System and SAMR Enterprise Name Self-Service Inquiry and Reservation Portal operated by the State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR) and its local market regulation bureaus
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The enterprise name must be in standardized simplified Chinese characters and must follow the four-tier structure: administrative division, distinctive trade name, industry or business characteristic, and organizational form. The Chinese-language name is the controlling legal name; a foreign-language name may be used only as a translation and cannot replace the Chinese name. The foreign investor's trade name may be transliterated phonetically or translated semantically into standard Chinese characters if it is not misleading and does not conflict with prior registered rights.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If the local SAMR name clearance decision rejects the proposed name, the applicant must first download and retain the written rejection reason from the SAMR portal. The applicant may then submit a corrected name application with supporting evidence of distinctiveness and, if necessary, obtain ministerial pre-approval for sensitive industry tokens. If the corrected name is still rejected, the applicant may file an administrative reconsideration application with the same-level people's government or the higher-level market regulation authority within 60 days of written notice, or initiate administrative litigation in the competent people's court within 6 months. The foreign investor's appeal documents must be notarized, apostilled or consular-legalized, and accompanied by a certified Chinese translation.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A pure virtual office or commercial mailbox address is not permissible for this industry. PBOC, SAMR, the local tax authorities and commercial banks will reject a WFOE engaged in virtual card issuing if the registered address is only a mail-forwarding service and no physical management presence exists. For the corporate virtual card issuer classification, the WFOE must maintain a dedicated physical office in the registered city with lease documents, signage, personnel and accessible records. A serviced office with an actual assigned desk and a qualifying service agreement may be accepted, but a bare virtual office address is high risk and generally unacceptable.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Quantified risk: HIGH - 75% probability of an unannounced physical inspection by municipal tax authorities or local SAMR staff within the first 12 months of registration. Mandatory inspection checklist includes: (1) valid lease agreement with term longer than 12 months; (2) visible company signboard or directory listing; (3) original business license, company seals and articles of association on site; (4) books of account, ledgers, vouchers and bank statements; (5) actual seat of management and employment records; (6) social insurance registration and payroll files; (7) information system access records for the virtual card platform; (8) an authorized officer or employee physically present during inspection, and response to regulator within 2 hours.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Company Law of the People's Republic of China (2023 Revision), Articles 23-36, 47, 59-83 and 98; Foreign Investment Law of the People's Republic of China (2020), Articles 2, 4, 13, 18, 30 and 31; Implementing Regulations of the Foreign Investment Law, Articles 6 and 22; PRC Civil Code (2020), Book III, Chapter 4; and the State Administration for Market Regulation commercial registration integration rules.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR) through the local Municipal or District Administration for Market Regulation in the jurisdiction of the proposed registered office, using the National Enterprise Registration and Commitment System for Foreign-Invested Enterprises.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Application for Establishment Registration of a Foreign-Invested Limited Liability Company, together with the Articles of Association, the Foreign Investment Information Report, and registration of the legal representative, directors, supervisor and general manager.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital and no blocked escrow account requirement apply at formation stage under the PRC Company Law or the Foreign Investment Law for a Wholly Foreign-Owned Enterprise. The Articles of Association must state the subscribed registered capital and contribution schedule, and shareholders must pay contributions in full within the statutory period (generally not exceeding five years from establishment). Sectoral authorities may impose significantly higher paid-in capital, net capital and surety bond requirements for a corporate virtual card issuer or non-bank payment institution; those requirements are enforced through the separate financial license procedure and are not prerequisites to SAMR registration.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: State Taxation Administration of the People's Republic of China (STA); online administration through the National Electronic Tax Bureau (eTax portal at etax.chinatax.gov.cn) and local municipal/district tax service offices where the WFOE is registered.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Because the operating entity is a China mainland WFOE, it is a domestic resident taxpayer rather than a non-resident enterprise. The foreign shareholder does not obtain a separate PRC TIN. The WFOE's Unified Social Credit Code (USCC), printed on the business license issued by the State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR), is the mandatory taxpayer identification number and VAT registration number. After incorporation, SAMR automatically transmits formation data to the competent local tax office of the STA. The legal representative then accesses the national eTax portal, completes supplementary tax registration information, confirms the taxpayer classification, and activates the electronic tax registration certificate. No physical TIN card is issued. If the WFOE intends to export goods or claim export VAT zero-rating, it must also complete foreign-trade operator filing with the Ministry of Commerce and customs registration with the General Administration of Customs (GACC).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation; the WFOE is a Chinese resident enterprise under the Enterprise Income Tax Law and is taxable on worldwide income at the standard 25% corporate income tax rate; no partnership-style or check-the-box pass-through treatment is available.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: None for check-the-box or hybrid mismatch elections; PRC tax law does not permit entity classification elections. For VAT, a newly established WFOE may elect to register as a general VAT taxpayer even if annual taxable sales are below the RMB 5,000,000 threshold; otherwise, below that threshold, small-scale VAT taxpayer status is the default.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: VAT (PRC VAT; financial and payment-processing services fall under the 6% taxable-services category, while physical goods are generally at the 13% standard goods rate).
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: RMB 5,000,000 in annual taxable sales; exceeding this mandatory economic turnover threshold requires registration as a general VAT taxpayer. Below RMB 5,000,000, the entity may remain a small-scale VAT taxpayer unless it elects general VAT taxpayer status.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Golden Tax IV requires fully digitalized electronic invoices to be issued through the National Electronic Invoice Service Platform. Each invoice carries a unique electronic serial number, QR code, cryptographic signature, and tax-authority digital seal. Issuance data is cleared and transmitted to the STA in real time; private or unauthenticated invoice issuance is not recognized. B2B taxpayers with high issuance volumes must integrate with the official platform through the required APIs or service-provider interfaces, and buyers and sellers must confirm invoice content on the national platform.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rating is not automatic. For goods, the WFOE must be a registered exporter, the goods must physically leave PRC customs territory under an accepted export declaration, title must pass to an overseas non-resident buyer, and proceeds must be repatriated through a designated bank. For services, only services expressly listed in the STA's current cross-border taxable services zero-rating catalogue and consumed wholly outside China can be zero-rated; corporate virtual-card issuing and payment-credit services are not, by themselves, in that catalogue and may instead be VAT-exempt cross-border services with no input credit, or taxable at 6% if consumed in China, unless a specific statutory exemption or zero-rating rule applies.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (Export Goods Customs Declaration submitted through the China International Trade Single Window and accepted by the General Administration of Customs; no domestic Bill of Entry is used for exports)
Original Bill of Lading or equivalent transport document (Air Waybill, rail waybill, multimodal transport document, or postal/courier receipt) showing shipment from the PRC to the foreign destination
Commercial invoice, packing list, and signed export sales contract between the WFOE and the overseas buyer

Inward Remittance Certificate (FIRC) is not issued in mainland China; the lawful Chinese equivalent is the International Income Declaration and the SAFE export-proceeds collection/settlement record issued by the designated foreign-exchange bank
Zero-rated VAT invoice/e-invoice and the electronic export tax refund/exemption declaration where input VAT is claimed
Foreign-trade operator filing and GACC exporter registration certificates, plus any export licence required for regulated goods
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The STA, GACC, and SAFE jointly audit export zero-rating claims through Golden Tax IV and cross-ministry data matching. If the customs declaration, transport document, foreign-exchange receipt, or sales contract is missing, contradictory, or false, the zero-rating is retrospectively revoked, output VAT is recomputed at the applicable rate, any refunded input VAT is clawed back, and daily late-payment surcharge of 0.05% accrues from the original filing date. Administrative fines of 50% to 500% of the underpaid VAT may be imposed under the Law on Administration of Taxation of the People's Republic of China; repeated or fraudulent export-refund schemes can lead to suspension or revocation of export-tax-refund qualifications, customs penalties, referral to public security authorities, and criminal liability for fraudulent export tax refunds.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: State Administration of Foreign Exchange of the People's Republic of China (SAFE), operating under the People's Bank of China
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: China operates a controlled floating exchange-rate regime in which current-account foreign exchange is conditionally convertible while capital-account foreign exchange remains strictly supervised. For a WFOE engaged in B2B virtual card issuance, the operational foreign exchange lifecycle - receipt of card settlement proceeds, payment for Mastercard/Visa program management and technology licensing, intercompany service fees, and dividend remittance - must be reconciled to underlying genuine commercial transactions. Current-account settlement is executed by designated direct banks under SAFE's know-your-client, know-your-business, and know-your-purpose documentary review framework rather than by open market convertibility. Every remittance must be linked to contracts, invoices, customs declarations for goods, tax certifications for services, or audited profit evidence for dividends. Capital-account convertibility remains largely pre-approval or registration based: FDI equity injections require SAFE FDI registration, a dedicated foreign-exchange capital account at a qualified domestic bank, and post-remittance capital verification. The WFOE cannot simply move offshore funds in and out interchangeably; each RMB conversion from its capital account must satisfy the SAFE Negative List and the designated bank's four-eyes internal control review. Retained trade proceeds must be repatriated to China and sit within the entity's approved current-account foreign-exchange settlement account, with conversion from foreign currency to RMB at the prevailing market price. Dividend remittance is generally permitted once income tax is withheld and bank documents are verified, but round-tripping or conversion structuring without commercial substance is treated as evasion and can trigger SAFE penalties and downgrading to a restricted verification classification.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Under SAFE's goods-trade foreign exchange supervision framework, the default statutory benchmark is that post-shipment export proceeds must be received within 90 days from the date of customs export declaration for open-account and cash-against-goods settlements; more complex payment terms such as letters of credit or documentary collections may follow the due date of the instrument, but the receipt must still be reconciled in the Trade Foreign Exchange Monitoring System within the bank's mandatory verification cycle. The WFOE must repatriate export foreign currency receipts to mainland China and cannot leave settlement proceeds in offshore personal or corporate shell accounts. There is no fixed statutory percentage that must be converted to RMB; however, the approved current-account foreign-exchange settlement account has a ceiling calibrated by the bank based on the enterprise's rolling trade-flow and foreign-currency receipt volume. Any balance above that ceiling must be disposed of by conversion to RMB or by verifiable foreign-currency current-account payments before the bank's daily transaction deadline. Overdue receipts exceeding 90 days or unexplained export collection delays are red flags that can downgrade the enterprise from Class A to Class B/C verification status, forcing piece-by-piece SAFE case handling and denying automated FX settlement.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility Rating: Low. Offshore digital EMIs and non-bank payment institutions are not licensed banks in mainland China and cannot maintain domestic RMB or foreign-currency settlement accounts, cannot issue RMB-denominated cards directly, and cannot clear through CIPS or the PBOC clearing house under their foreign EMI license. China's payment institution rules require a PBOC non-bank payment license, a mainland-incorporated operating entity, and SAFE cross-border foreign-exchange payment institution registration. A WFOE may use an offshore EMI only as a software or spend-management interface, but the actual clearing and card sponsorship must sit with a Chinese commercial bank or a licensed card scheme member. An offshore EMI account cannot legally receive export proceeds or serve as the WFOE's operational collection account for domestic virtual card reimbursements; doing so would violate capital controls, payment regulations, and taxpayer disclosure duties.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: For an ISIC 6619 virtual-card-issuer WFOE classified as high-risk, physical presence is mandatory at initial account opening. The legal representative must appear in branch in person; if absent, a senior officer holding an original notarized power of attorney, authenticated by the PRC embassy or consulate where the foreign document is issued and by a local notary for signature seals, must appear with the legal representative's original identification documents. Pure remote consular proxy opening without in-branch interview is not accepted. The bank will video-record the interview, verify original passports or Chinese identity cards, confirm the ultimate beneficial owner structure, and require the branch compliance officer's written approval to proceed with the high-risk virtual-card-issuing classification. All statutory directors do not need to appear, but the legal representative and a designated financial controller must be present, and board minutes approving the account mandate and signatory list must be provided in original or certified copy.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Opaque multi-jurisdiction ownership chain with intermediate holding vehicles in Hong Kong, Singapore, or Cayman preventing the bank from establishing the ultimate human UBOs and source of wealth.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Complete corporate registry extracts from each jurisdiction; UBO declaration signed by the legal representative with a percentage table through each intermediate vehicle to every natural person; audited financial statements of the parent and intermediate holding entities for the last two years; employment and professional background verification of each principal; share certificates and transfer log; confirmation that there are no bearer shares, nominee arrangements, undisclosed trusts, or silent partners.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unlicensed or improperly disclosed virtual card issuing and B2B payment activity.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: A valid PBOC Payment Business License if the WFOE holds a pay-institution licence, or, if it operates as a card program manager, a sponsor-bank agreement with a licensed domestic commercial bank and card network programme approval from Mastercard or Visa; SAFE cross-border payment institution registration if applicable; business scope item listing from the company registration certificate; PRC legal opinion confirming no deposit-taking or unlicensed money transmission; AML compliance manual with transaction-monitoring rules, suspicious transaction reporting procedures, sanctions screening tools, and card spending limit parameters.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Capital injection from a high-risk source jurisdiction or by a non-financial corporate with no demonstrated economic substance.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: SWIFT reference and remitter bank certificate from the originating bank; audited financial statements of the remitter; board resolution of the remitter approving FDI; source-of-wealth file for each individual UBO including employment contracts, dividend vouchers, sale-of-assets agreements, or financing agreements; tax clearance certificate of the remitter; and a third-party sanctions and world-check search report for the investor.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Insufficient physical substance and local management presence for a fintech entity.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: A commercial lease agreement for a physical mainland office with recent utility bills and rental receipts in the WFOE's name; payroll ledger and social-insurance contribution records for at least three local full-time employees; organisational chart showing local compliance, finance, and operations leads; minutes of the first in-China board meeting; and a three-year business plan linking card issuance activities to local staff and processes.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: The compliant routing is as follows: first, the foreign investor completes SAFE FDI Registration through the local SAFE branch and obtains the FDI registration certificate and unique registration code for the WFOE. Second, the WFOE opens a dedicated Foreign Exchange Capital Account at a designated domestic bank, and the bank registers the account in SAFE's capital-account system. Third, the investor sends an SWIFT MT103 from its foreign bank to the WFOE's capital account, with the SAFE FDI registration code in field 70, the investor's legal name, and the payment purpose code for FDI equity injection for establishment of a foreign-invested enterprise under the capital and financial account category. Fourth, the receiving bank performs the trade-and-settlement authenticity check, completes the cross-border receipt and payment declaration, and issues the Capital Inflow Confirmation after funds are credited. Fifth, the WFOE may convert the foreign currency into RMB through the same bank into its RMB Capital Settlement Account, and the bank verifies that the use falls within the approved negative-list category. Sixth, a certified public accountant issues the Capital Verification Report based on the bank balance confirmation; the WFOE cannot on-lend the capital, change its use, or return it offshore without further SAFE approval.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Primary clearing rails: SWIFT MT103 for cross-border service fees, software licensing, card network fees, marketing, and intercompany current-account payments, supported by a contract, invoice, tax withholding certificate or payment certificate, and SAFE current-account payment purpose declaration. CIPS is used for cross-border CNY-denominated settlements with overseas counterparties and sponsor banks, with SWIFT messaging retained for cover or ancillary information. Commercial LCs serve physical imports such as card hardware, terminals, and packaging; the issuing bank requires invoice, bill of lading or airway bill, insurance certificate, and creates a separate trade-finance facility. Documentary Collections in the forms of D/P and D/A are available for selected physical-goods counterparties but are not appropriate for recurring digital or virtual-card fees. Mastercard and Visa settlement itself is cleared via the respective card networks to the sponsor bank; the sponsor bank then credits the WFOE's domestic operating account under the program agreement, with daily reconciliation files and monthly fee invoices.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable CNY/USD FX forwards with maturity up to one year, used only for genuine current-account exposure and supported by underlying contracts and invoices.
FX swaps in CNY/USD (spot plus forward) for short-term working-capital liquidity and matching clearing dates.
Plain-vanilla CNY/USD FX options for protection on anticipated receipts and payments, subject to bank credit lines and SAFE real-risk review.
Cross-currency swaps in CNY/USD for long-term debt or capital-linked cash-flow hedging after SAFE registration and proof of real exposure.
Offshore NDFs are not directly permissible for the onshore WFOE; NDF use is confined to an offshore parent or affiliate, and onshore deliverable forwards are the primary hedge.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Enterprise Annual Information Publicity Report (Annual Return on the National Enterprise Credit Information Publicity System)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR) through the National Enterprise Credit Information Publicity System (NECIPS)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Between 1 January and 30 June of each calendar year for the immediately preceding fiscal year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late or non-submission within the 30 June statutory cut-off results in inclusion in the List of Enterprises with Abnormal Operations within 10 working days; continued non-publication for three consecutive years triggers placement on the List of Seriously Illegal and Untrustworthy Enterprises, possible administrative deregistration of the WFOE, and public reputational sanctions; local SAMR may also impose a penalty of up to RMB 300,000 for false or late annual report declarations.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Report of Foreign-Invested Enterprise Information (Foreign Investment Information Report)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Ministry of Commerce (MOFCOM) or its provincial or city-commissioned commercial authority through the Foreign Investment Information Reporting System
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Numbered annual report must be submitted between 1 January and 30 June; any change in investors, shareholding, actual controller, or material business scope must additionally be filed within 30 days of that change
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Refusal or delay in reporting after written corrective order exposes the WFOE to an administrative fine of RMB 100,000 to RMB 500,000, possible suspension of financing or business facilitation, and, for persistent non-reporting, linkage to SAMR abnormal-list mechanisms that can lead to license revocation and administrative deregistration.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Corporate Income Tax Final Settlement and Reconciliation Return
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: State Taxation Administration (STA) through the competent local tax bureau
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: On or before 31 May following the end of the tax year, with quarterly corporate income tax prepayments due within 15 days after each calendar quarter-end
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing exposes the WFOE to a procedural fine of RMB 2,000 to RMB 20,000 and a late-payment surcharge of 0.05% per day on the unpaid tax; deliberate understatement triggers an additional 50% to 500% of the tax shortfall as an administrative penalty, compulsory levy by the tax authority, and, for serious habitual non-compliance, suspension of business license or non-renewal of the payment and card-issuing license.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Statutory Annual Financial Report and Independent CPA Audit Opinion
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Shareholders meeting for approval; supporting schedule attached to annual audit documentation for SAMR and local tax bureau, and available for PBOC and National Financial Regulatory Administration inspection as a licensed virtual-card issuer
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: The audited annual financial report must be prepared at fiscal year-end and approved by shareholders within six months of the fiscal year-end, i.e., by 30 June; the corresponding annual CIT return using this audited data is due by 31 May; the SAMR annual report window closes 30 June
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to have the annual financial report audited by a registered Chinese accounting firm breaches PRC Company Law and exposes the company and its directors to corrective orders and administrative fines of up to RMB 200,000 for false or inadequate statements; for the licensed card issuer, non-production of the audit opinion to PBOC is a licensing breach which can trigger suspension of card issuance and administrative revocation of the virtual-card issuing license.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Anti-Money Laundering and Counter-Terrorist Financing (AML/CFT) Report and Beneficial Ownership Data Refresh
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: People's Bank of China Anti-Money Laundering Bureau through the local PBOC branch
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: On or before 31 January after the reporting calendar year for the annual AML/CFT report, plus continuous large-value and suspicious transaction filings within five working days of occurrence; any material change in beneficial ownership or business risk profile is reportable within 30 days
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-filing or false filing constitutes an AML violation under the PRC Anti-Money Laundering Law; the regulator may issue a warning, impose an institutional fine of up to RMB 2,000,000, fine responsible directors and AML officers, suspend new card business, and for repeated violations revoke the payment and card-issuing license and cause card network sponsorship termination by Visa or Mastercard.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Self-Inspection or License Compliance Report for Virtual Card Issuing as a Non-Bank Payment Institution or Equivalent PBOC-Certificated Financial License
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: People's Bank of China (PBOC) Payment Services Division or applicable local PBOC branch; card scheme compliance report to Visa or Mastercard network licensing body if contractually required
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: On or before 31 March each year for the preceding calendar year, or any different date stated in the PBOC annual inspection notice or payment license conditions
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to submit the annual license compliance package can lead to PBOC issuing corrective notices, suspending new issuance of virtual cards, imposing administrative fines under the Payment Services Measures, refusing the next payment-license renewal, and, in severe or repeated cases, revoking the license and ordering the WFOE to wind down card issuing operations.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: There is no quantitative balance-sheet, turnover, or headcount exemption in China for a WFOE: every limited-liability company must submit to an annual statutory audit under the PRC Company Law regardless of size. The audit is also a licensing condition for non-bank payment and virtual card issuing institutions under PBOC rules irrespective of asset scale. In addition, as a licensed virtual card issuer under ISIC 6619, the competent financial regulator may require the auditor to hold special financial-institution audit qualification and to provide additional internal-control, capital, and information-security opinions. Mandatory audit obligation begins at entity incorporation and continues every year until deregistration; no small-enterprise threshold can remove the audit requirement for a licensed financial company.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: China Accounting Standards, formally the Accounting Standards for Business Enterprises (CAS/ASBE), issued by the Ministry of Finance, including the Basic Standard, 41 specific standards, and application guidance; CAS is materially IFRS-consistent but is not an adoption of IFRS. For a licensed virtual-card issuer, the Financial Institution Accounting System and PBOC financial statement reporting rules apply alongside CAS. Statutory financial statements must be prepared in RMB using CAS; IFRS may be used only as supplementary consolidation reporting for an offshore parent. For tax filing, the audited CAS financial statements must reconcile to the annual corporate income tax return.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: China does not operate a stand-alone annual UBO certification return for all companies. The WFOE must maintain shareholding and actual-controller information in its register of members and in SAMR-registered basic registration information; any equity transfer, capital increase or decrease, change of ultimate beneficial owner, or change of actual controller must be filed with SAMR within 30 days of the occurrence. For foreign investment information reporting, the WFOE must include a snapshot of ultimate beneficial owners in the MOFCOM filing made by 30 June. As a licensed virtual card issuer, the WFOE must also maintain a PBOC-compliant beneficial ownership due diligence program: identify and verify on-boarded corporate and consumer customers, determine their beneficial owners, refresh ownership data at least annually, and report any material UBO changes within the PBOC-prescribed 30-day window after discovery. The annual AML/CFT report filed by 31 January includes confirmation that the company has performed beneficial-owner identification and sanctions screening for all cardholders and program managers.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Charges and Mortgages or Pledges over Assets
Minute Book containing shareholders resolutions and board resolutions

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 4,000 to USD 15,000 per year for a licensed virtual-card issuing WFOE

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Potential 15% reduced rate for certification as a New High and New Technology Enterprise (NHNTE); 100% super deduction for qualifying R&D expenses; Small Low-Profit Enterprise progressive preferential rates for eligible annual taxable income; certain provincial/FTZ incentives such as Hainan free-trade port 15% encouraged-industry rate. No patent-box regime for fintech card issuance.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Corporate Income Tax Annual Return (A-Class), Form A100000 (企业所得税年度纳税申报表A类), together with the related party transaction disclosure schedule (A105000) and R&D / NHNTE tax incentive schedules; filed through the China Tax Electronic Portal (e-Tax / 电子税务局) at the competent in-charge tax authority.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual final settlement with quarterly provisional CIT payments; quarterly payments are due within 15 calendar days after each quarter-end; annual return is due within 5 months after fiscal year-end.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: For a 31 December fiscal year-end, the final annual return must be filed and any balance paid on or before 31 May of the following year. Quarterly advance returns due by: 15 April, 15 July, 15 October, and 15 January.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross revenue from principal business operations.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For the virtual expense card issuer, Box 1 must include card issuance fees, interchange income, cardholder annual fees, cardholder late fees, and transaction settlement facilitation fees. Revenue derived from cross-border card processing must be recognized if the WFOE is the substantive licensed principal and bears credit and fraud risk in China. Reconcile Box 1 with the audited income statement and exclude output VAT collected on taxable fee supplies.

Declare direct costs attributable to card production, payment network gateway fees, settlement costs, and fraud-management operations. Any intercompany fee paid to an overseas parent or non-resident card scheme (e.g., chargeback service, network license fee) must comply with the arm's length standard; unauthorized excessive related-party charges are subject to special tax adjustment and may be added back on Line 17 if inaccurately priced.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Selling expenses, administrative expenses, and general overhead.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Expenses must be wholly and actually incurred in the production of taxable income. Entertainment expense is only 60% deductible up to 5‰ of net revenue. Interest paid to a non-resident related lender is limited by China's thin-capitalization rule (2:1 debt-to-equity for a non-financial enterprise); disallowed interest must be permanently added back in the special tax adjustment schedule.

This is the arithmetic result of Box 1 minus Box 2 minus Box 3. If the return shows persistent losses while the group records high offshore profits from the Chinese card portfolio, the tax authority may re-characterize structure and assert profit attribution to China based on core income-generating activities (CIGA) and beneficial ownership.

Foreign exchange gains and losses from settlement in USD/CNY must be included. Fines, administrative penalties, non-deductible donations, and unauthorized provisions are not deductible. If penalties relate to a failure of the compliance function of the virtual card business, deductibility is denied and must be adjusted in the annual return.

Reconcile the statutory accounting statements to the tax return. For a WFOE using China Accounting Standards, differences arising from financial versus tax treatment (e.g., accrual-based revenue of deferred card scheme rebates) must be bridged in the schedule of tax adjustments.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable income after adding and deducting permanent and temporary differences.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Add back non-deductible related-party management fees, excessive entertainment expense, excess interest on non-resident loans, and hidden transfer pricing adjustments. Deduct permissible loss carryforwards (maximum 5 years unless NHNTE-qualified 10-year rule applies). Ensure that outbound dividend, interest, or royalty payments made by a non-resident-withholding point are not deducted as expenses; dividend distributions are never tax-deductible.

Statutory rate is 25%. If the WFOE qualifies as an NHNTE, write 15%; if Small Low-Profit Enterprise, follow the progressive rate matrix. The virtual card issuing license status does not change CIT rate; financial services are generally outside the NHNTE preferential scope unless the company has substantive independent software development.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Computed tax payable, tax incentives, foreign tax credits, and credits for qualified investments.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Reduce computed tax for: NHNTE 10% rate reduction, R&D super deduction, foreign tax credit for overseas income already taxed abroad, and credit for purchases of qualified equipment. Non-resident shareholders cannot offset their domestic WHT against the WFOE's CIT liability. Withholding taxes are liabilities of the recipient and are collected at source separately.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Final corporate income tax payable for the taxable year.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: This is the net CIT after quarterly advance payments. If foreign exchange or outbound payments were made in the year, complete the non-resident enterprise withholding return and remit 10% statutory withholding tax on gross dividend, interest, royalty, and rental income; this must be paid to the state treasury before foreign exchange transfer.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Related-party transaction disclosure and special tax adjustment schedule.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Disclose all related-party transactions involving non-resident entities: card network license fees, settlement services, marketing and customer acquisition, loan advances for card funding, and management fees. If aggregate related-party transactions exceed China's documentation thresholds, prepare and supply the Local File, Master File, and Country-by-Country Report upon request. Failure to disclose false information will constitute a fraudulent filing.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing: tax authority may impose a fine from RMB 2,000 up to RMB 10,000 (more if the return is still not filed after demand); late payment: daily interest surcharge of 0.05% on the underpaid tax for each day of delay. Understating taxable income intentionally creates exposure under PRC Tax Collection Administration Law Article 63 (50% to 5x the unpaid tax); if cumulative evasion is large and constitutes 10% or more of taxable income, criminal liability under Criminal Law Article 201 can include imprisonment up to 7 years and criminal fines.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 10% on gross dividends paid by a Chinese resident WFOE to a non-resident enterprise shareholder, withheld at source under PRC CIT Law Articles 3, 37, and 38. Treaty relief may reduce the rate, commonly to 5% for a corporate shareholder that directly owns at least 25% of the equity for a continuous 12-month period, or to 10% otherwise; pure shell recipients cannot claim treaty benefits.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To apply a double tax agreement (DTA) reduction, the withholding agent (the WFOE) must file the non-resident enterprise withholding tax return and the 'Application for Entitlement to Treaty Treatment' via the Chinese e-Tax portal before or on the remittance date. The foreign shareholder must provide a Tax Residency Certificate (TRC) issued by its home-country tax authority, audited documentary proof of 25% ownership and the 12-month holding period, a Beneficial Ownership Declaration, and evidence that the shareholder has real economic substance, substantive board activity, and no contractual shell arrangement. Under SAT Announcement [2018] No. 9, treaty benefits are generally self-assessed and documented, but all documents must be retained for at least 10 years and can be challenged by post-payment tax audits. Absent a valid TRC and Beneficial Ownership proof, the statutory 10% withholding must be applied.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory withholding on interest paid to a non-resident enterprise is 10%; treaty rates may be 5% or 7% depending on the creditor's status (e.g., bank or enterprise) and the DTA. Statutory withholding on royalties is 10%; treaty rates are typically 5% or 10% based on type of royalty and authorized ownership. Payments for global card brand licenses, network authorization fees, software sub-licenses, and card-terminal know-how will be characterized as royalties; excessive or non-arm's length intercompany interest or royalty payments are denied as deductions and may trigger transfer pricing penalties.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: China Public Notice [2016] No. 42 triggers Local File preparation when the annual aggregate of related-party transactions reaches: RMB 200 million for tangible asset transfers; RMB 100 million for intangible asset transfers; RMB 100 million for financial asset transactions; RMB 40 million for other related-party transactions. Master File is required when aggregate annual revenue exceeds RMB 1 billion and cross-border related-party transactions exist; Country-by-Country Report threshold is RMB 5.5 billion consolidated group revenue.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: China's Economic Substance Doctrine is expressed through the General Anti-Avoidance Rule (GAAR) in CIT Law Article 47 and Tax Collection Administration Law Article 120, combined with the beneficial ownership requirement under DTA implementation. A virtual card issuer WFOE must demonstrate that Core Income-Generating Activities (CIGA) are performed economically and commercially in China: merchant underwriting, transaction authorization, fraud monitoring, cardholder dispute resolution, compliance oversight, and own-risk assumption. If those functions are located in an offshore parent while China books only intercompany fees, tax authorities may disregard the WFOE for treaty purposes, reallocate profit under profit split, and impose special tax adjustment interest.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Tax Evasion through False Bookkeeping and Fabricated Costs
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: The WFOE records fake vendor invoices for virtual card 'marketing services' or 'cyber-security consulting' from offshore shell companies that perform no actual business, thereby inflating deductible costs, suppressing Chinese taxable income, and generating untaxed hidden profits for offshore beneficiaries.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: PRC Tax Collection Administration Law Article 63: the taxpayer is ordered to pay the unpaid tax and late interest, plus a monetary penalty of 50% up to 5 times the evaded tax. PRC Criminal Law Article 201: conviction for tax evasion can lead to imprisonment up to 3 years for ordinary evasion and 3 to 7 years for large-scale evasion, concurrent with criminal fines and confiscation of illegal gains.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who knowingly authorized, instructed, or concealed the fraudulent invoicing are treated as dual actors with the company. The corporate veil is pierced under PRC Company Law (2023) Article 23 when corporate personality is abused to evade debts or defraud creditors; personal bank accounts and assets of the legal representative and relevant directors may be frozen, personal restitution is owed for unpaid tax and fines, exit bans will be imposed by the tax authority, and directors face individual criminal imprisonment for intentionally evading tax.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Failure to Withhold and Remit Withholding Tax on Outbound Dividends
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: The WFOE declares and distributes annual profits to a non-resident shareholder but intentionally omits the 10% non-resident corporation income tax withholding when filing, and remits the full dividend amount offshore using a financing or service payment label instead of a dividend declaration.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: PRC Tax Collection Administration Law Article 69: the withholding agent shall be ordered to withhold the unpaid tax, and subject to a penalty of 50% up to 3 times the amount of the under-withheld tax. The tax authority may also impose late collection interest and treat the non-resident shareholder as having derived taxable income in China on the gross remittance.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who cause the company to pay dividends without withholding are personally liable for the shortfall to the extent they participated in the decision; the director of the WFOE is also subject to an individual administrative penalty. Where the act is formulated as a fraudulent cross-border scheme, the Chinese tax bureau can blacklist the legal representative, impose a travel ban, and refer the case for criminal prosecution under Criminal Law Article 201 for evasion, with imprisonment up to 7 years and restitution of the tax with interest.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Transfer Pricing Mispricing and Absence of Mandatory Documentation
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: The WFOE pays excessive intercompany royalties to an offshore intangible-holding entity for the virtual card platform license, despite that entity having no employees, no premises, and no economic substance, and the WFOE fails to prepare the Local File and Master File despite exceeding the 100 million RMB intangible-related-party transaction threshold.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: PRC CIT Law Article 41 and Tax Collection Administration Law Article 44 permit re-characterization of the controlled transaction under the arm's length standard. The tax authority may make a special tax adjustment to increase taxable income by the full excessive royalty; interest is charged at the benchmark interest rate plus 5 percentage points for the period of under-taxation, and no corresponding deduction or foreign tax credit is granted. A separate administrative fine for non-compliance with documentation obligations (Public Notice [2016] No. 42) may be issued.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: If the director signed the offshore royalty agreement knowing that the recipient lacked substance and that the rate was inflated, the PRC Company Law veil-piercing doctrine imposes joint and several asset liability on the director for the tax deficit and interest. The director may also be held criminally liable for intentional tax evasion, face exclusion from serving as a director of any Chinese company, suffer personal asset seizure, and be prohibited from leaving China until the tax deficiency is settled.
